title: Qwen3-30B-A3B (Instruct)
name: Qwen3-30B-A3B (Instruct)
description: Qwen3-30B-A3B (Instruct) is the cost-efficiency point in Qwen3’s MoE line: 30.5B total parameters with only 3.3B active per token, which makes it materially cheaper to serve than the flagship 235B-A22B while retaining the family’s thinking/non-thinking controls and agent-oriented behavior. It is the variant to choose when you want reasoning-capable production inference on constrained hardware, but cannot justify the memory and throughput cost of the larger MoE checkpoint. The engineering trade-off is straightforward: lower serving cost and easier scaling than the flagship model, but less absolute reasoning headroom and long-context robustness than the top-end checkpoint.

hardware.recommended_gpu: NVIDIA RTX 4090 / A5000 / A6000-class or similar high-memory consumer/workstation GPU

deployment.recommended_quantization: AWQ or GPTQ for production cost reduction when quality validation passes; BF16 only if you can afford the larger memory footprint and need maximum fidelity.

best_for: Cost-efficient reasoning services with explicit thinking/non-thinking behavior.
Tool-using agents where lower active-parameter cost matters more than flagship-model headroom.
Quantized single-node or small-cluster deployment where budget is constrained but quality still matters.
avoid_for: Highest-stakes reasoning workloads that justify the flagship 235B-A22B MoE model.
Ultra-low-latency workloads that need a tiny dense model instead of MoE routing.
Teams that cannot validate quantization effects on reasoning quality before rollout.
engineering_snapshot.recommended_use_case: Production reasoning and agent serving with constrained compute budgets.
deployment_risks: Treating Qwen3-30B-A3B as a dense-model memory problem. MoE serving amplifies configuration mistakes, so plan for MoE routing and quantization strategy early.
Enabling YaRN by default for all traffic.
failure_modes: KeyError: 'qwen3_moe' when using a Transformers version older than 4.51.0.
Degraded short-text performance if YaRN is enabled unnecessarily.
common_mistakes: Enabling YaRN by default for all traffic rather than only applying long-context scaling to requests that need it.
operational_notes: The official model card recommends enable_thinking=True by default and documents the <think>...</think> output structure for reasoning mode.

For thinking mode, the official defaults are Temperature=0.6, TopP=0.95, TopK=20, MinP=0, and the model card explicitly warns against greedy decoding because it can degrade performance and cause repetition.
The official model card recommends max_new_tokens=32768 for most queries and up to 38912 for especially hard math/programming tasks.
The official model card recommends vLLM and SGLang as deployment targets, and provides concrete serving flags for both.
YaRN is supported for long contexts, but the official docs warn that static YaRN can degrade shorter-text performance; only enable it when your workload needs >32K context.
In practice, this checkpoint rewards careful output-length and KV-cache planning more than dense 30B-class models because MoE serving amplifies configuration mistakes.
Prefer quantized serving for cost control, but validate reasoning-sensitive tasks before promoting INT4/INT3-style reductions to production.
Preserve the model’s thinking/non-thinking switch in your middleware so you do not collapse the performance/latency trade-off the family was designed to expose.
Variant differentiation (Identity): compared with dense 32B-class variants, this model is MoE-based and therefore materially changes deployment economics by activating only 3.3B parameters per token.

Variant differentiation (Specifications): the official model card exposes the 48-layer, 128-expert / 8-active-expert MoE configuration, which is the key reason this checkpoint sits in a different serving class than dense Qwen3 models.

Variant differentiation (File Formats): GGUF is especially relevant here because the 30B/3B active footprint is small enough to be practical for local quantized workflows, unlike the flagship MoE model that is typically cluster-first.

Variant differentiation (Hardware Requirements): this is the most deployable Qwen3 MoE checkpoint for cost-sensitive production, and hardware planning is mostly about whether you want quantized single-GPU service or BF16 multi-GPU service.
Variant differentiation (Downloads): use the Hugging Face model card for checkpoint-specific serving notes and the Qwen download portal for canonical distribution paths and quantized artifacts.

Variant differentiation (Runtime Compatibility): the runtime story is strongest for vLLM and SGLang because the official docs expose reasoning-mode controls directly, which matters for this instruct checkpoint’s behavior contract.

Variant differentiation (Deployment): the 30B-A3B instruct checkpoint is the best fit when you need reasoning-quality MoE behavior but want a materially smaller active-parameter budget than the flagship model.
Variant differentiation (License): license terms do not materially distinguish this variant from the rest of the family; deployment economics are the differentiator.
Variant differentiation (Status): this checkpoint is released as an active production model, not a research-only artifact, and remains part of the current Qwen3 deployment stack.
Variant relationship (Qwen3-235B-A22B): Larger flagship MoE sibling with higher reasoning headroom and much heavier serving requirements.
Variant relationship (Qwen3-32B): Dense alternative with simpler deployment mechanics but no MoE efficiency benefit.
Variant relationship (Qwen3-14B): Smaller dense sibling for lower-cost deployments where 30B-A3B is too heavy.
